one_line: Meta acquires AI coding startup Conductor, while new releases include Qualcomm's AI accelerator, a document-to-JSON field extractor, StateBench for long-document tracking, and Palette for automated slide generation.

stories.title: Meta Acquires AI Coding Startup Conductor
stories.summary: Meta has acquired the AI coding startup Conductor, which was founded in 2024 by Charlie Holtz. Following the acquisition, Conductor's cloud service is scheduled to shut down on November 20.
stories.why_it_matters: Developers relying on Conductor's cloud service must migrate away before it shuts down on November 20.
stories.editor_reason: Meta acquires AI coding startup Conductor to boost agentic software engineering.

stories.title: Dharma Field Extractor Converts Document Images to Structured JSON
stories.summary: Developers built a 2-billion-parameter model called the Field Extractor that takes document images and returns structured JSON based on open requests or specific schemas. The base model used is DharmaOCR-LITE v1.1, which was trained with a LoRA adapter on 43,384 training examples across three data streams.
stories.why_it_matters: You can use this model to extract structured JSON directly from document images based on specific schemas.
stories.editor_reason: Hugging Face releases Dharma Field Extractor for structured JSON output from documents.

facts.claim: The developers built a 2-billion-parameter model called the Field Extractor that takes document images and returns structured JSON based on open requests or specific schemas.
facts.quote: A 2-billion-parameter model that extracts exactly the fields you ask for, from any document type

facts.claim: The base model used is DharmaOCR-LITE v1.1, which was trained with a LoRA adapter on 43,384 training examples across three data streams.
facts.quote: The base model is DharmaOCR-LITE v1.1, a new 2-billion-parameter version optimized from the one in the paper and already specialized for OCR through supervised fine-tuning and DPO.

stories.title: Hugging Face Introduces StateBench for Long-Document Tracking
stories.summary: Hugging Face introduced StateBench, a new benchmark with four difficulty levels designed to evaluate how language models track evolving entity information in long documents. Researchers found that frontier models, including specific versions of Gemini, Claude, and GPT, still struggle and break down on harder forms of state tracking as input lengths increase.
stories.why_it_matters: You need to be aware that current frontier language models struggle with complex state tracking over long inputs when building or using AI applications.
stories.editor_reason: New StateBench evaluates how language models track state changes over long documents.

facts.claim: Hugging Face introduced StateBench, a new benchmark designed to evaluate how well language models track information about entities as they evolve in long documents.
facts.quote: We’re introducing StateBench, a benchmark for long-context state tracking—how well language models keep track of information about entities in long documents as they evolve.

facts.claim: StateBench features four distinct difficulty levels for state update operations: r-trivial, aperiodic, soluble, and general finite.
facts.quote: StateBench consists of four difficulty levels that permit increasingly complex state update operations.

facts.claim: Researchers found that frontier models, including specific versions of Gemini, Claude, and GPT, still struggle and break down on harder forms of state tracking as input lengths increase.
facts.quote: frontier models including Gemini 3.8 Flash, Claude Opus 5.5, and GPT-6 Sol and Luna still break down on harder forms of state tracking as inputs grow longer.

facts.claim: The evaluation tested open pretrained models including 7-billion-parameter models Olmo 3 (a transformer) and Olmo Hybrid (featuring Gated DeltaNet layers).
facts.quote: These included two 7-billion-parameter models, Olmo 3 (a transformer) and Olmo Hybrid (which adds Gated DeltaNet layers), along with smaller models with 275 million and 2.7 billion parameters.

stories.title: Palette Fine-Tunes 20B Model for Design-Compliant Slide Generation
stories.summary: Researchers fine-tuned a 20B open-weight model named Palette on synthetic data following the IBM Design Language, allowing it to rank first on two of three PresentBench domains. Because slide contexts are fixed beforehand, its parallelized coding stage runs roughly 6 to 7 times faster.
stories.why_it_matters: You can leverage Palette to generate design-compliant slide decks efficiently using a 20B open-weight model trained on specific styling rules.
stories.editor_reason: Palette teaches small models to build presentation decks in custom design languages.

facts.claim: Researchers fine-tuned a 20B open-weight model called Palette to build slide decks following a specific design language.
facts.quote: We fine-tuned a 20B model to build decks the way people do: a designer plans the deck and a coder draws each slide.

facts.claim: Palette's training data follows the IBM Design Language, allowing it to rank first on two out of three domains on PresentBench.
facts.quote: Its training data follows the IBM Design Language, and on PresentBench it ranks first on two of the three domains we measured.

facts.claim: Because slide contexts are fixed beforehand, the coding stage runs in parallel and is approximately 6 to 7 times faster.
facts.quote: the coder calls run in parallel, one per slide, which makes the coding stage about 6–7× faster.

facts.claim: The researchers generated synthetic training data consisting of around 1,000 decks covering roughly 10,000 slides using a large open teacher.
facts.quote: We generated around 1000 decks covering roughly 10,000 slides.
